issues.note: Confirmed in the frozen sources: r00002 ends with the first word of a two-word epithet in both languages and r00003 begins with the second, so the two rows should be one. The author prepared but withheld the join because r00003/ar carries a recorded punctuation normalization and the pinned test tests/runtime-audio.test.ts (lines 156 to 158) requires a built field to equal one mapped piece. I hit the same limit on my own items. This needs the coordinator's test change; nothing further is asked of the author.

Checked: the last Persian piece of r00003 has no Arabic in r00003 and renders exactly the first Arabic piece of r00004, which has no Persian in r00004. The exact merge puts the two together; no characters touch, so no space is needed.

Checked both parts. The exact pairing with r00003/fa is right. The join of the final piece with the head of r00005 is right in content and both spaces are correct. The resulting row is long; a shorter division was tried and is not possible without a mapping migration, see the note on r00004/ar.

layout.note: Read all 120 output rows in both languages. Every paired row holds an Arabic piece and its own Persian rendering; the heading, note and two instruction rows are Persian only. Four cross-row joins are in place and correct: the exact pairing of r00003/fa with r00004/ar, and the joins r00004 with r00005, r00007 with r00008 and r00011 with r00012. Three boundaries still split a phrase across rows (r00002 with r00003, r00006 with r00007, r00014 with r00015); they are correctly identified and are blocked by the pinned test, not by the author. One merged row is long and cannot be re-cut without a mapping migration; accepted, see r00004/ar.
